g.text: MHA vs MQA vs GQA vs MLA: one comparison sheet
Explained on: Beyond → Attention variants compared · sessions 02, 04 MQA, 05 GQA, 06 MLA | M_KV = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S
1. Head wiring side by side (8 of 32 query heads drawn; arrows = which cached K/V a head reads)
head i: O_i = softmax( Q_i K_i^T / sqrt(d_h) ) V_i
head i: O_i = softmax( Q_i K^T / sqrt(d_h) ) V (same K, V)
head i in group g: softmax( Q_i K_g^T / sqrt(d_h) ) V_g
q.k = (c^Q)^T W^UQT W^UK c^KV absorbed; + RoPE path
Q diverse, KV shared per group.
GQA = head sharing | MLA = representation compression (a learned low-rank latent + a separate RoPE path)
toy = L=32, H_q=32, d_h=64, FP16, T=100K, B=1 | Llama-shape = L=32, H_q=32, d_h=128, BF16 (Llama-3-8B: H_kv=8) | MLA = DeepSeek-V2 numbers (L=60)
Llama-3-8B: 2*32*8*128*2 B = 131,072 B = 128 KiB; 8K tokens = 1 GiB per sequence.
MLA: 576 * 2 B * 60 layers = 69,120 B (67.5 KiB) per token vs 3.75 MiB if it were MHA (32,768 * 2 B * 60).
decode AI = H_q/H_kv (FLOP/B) vs A100 ridge ~200: all memory-bound.
it trades bytes for FLOPs and lands near the ridge.
DeepSeek-V2: 93.3% KV reduction vs DeepSeek 67B, 5.76x max throughput.
3. Which term of M_KV = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S does each technique attack?
K and V rebuilt from ONE
Hybrid SSM: only 1/8 layers have KV
-> more B fits in same VRAM
(M ~ W not T; lose distant tokens)
MLA attacks H_kv * d_h TOGETHER (DeepSeek-V2, n_h = d_h = 128):
old systems used 20.4-38.2% of KV memory for real tokens;
vLLM waste < 4% (last partial block). Math size M_KV unchanged.
NOT in the formula (prefill cost): prefix caching
1000 users sharing a 2K-token system prompt prefill it ONCE.
attacks TTFT and FLOPs, not the per-token cache size.
NOT in the formula (bandwidth): FlashAttention, fused kernels
reduce HBM traffic / T x T materialisation;
raise AI without shrinking the cache.
4. Quality vs efficiency: MLA is OFF the one-dimensional line
A 1-D 'diversity' axis fails for MLA: it does not reduce
head count, it changes WHAT is cached (a learned low-rank
latent c^KV, up-projected to per-head K/V when needed).
So a good MLA can sit above the MHA->MQA curve.
TRADE-OFF: GQA/MQA trade quality for bytes along a curve;
hybrids trade exact retrieval for state; MLA pays in
GQA vs MLA at equal budget: MLA's 576 elements per
token per layer = GQA with 2.25 KV groups (d_h=128),
but MLA keeps 128 distinct per-head K/V views.
5. Retrofit levels: what does adoption cost?
MHA -> GQA (cheap): K_g = (1/n) * sum_{i in g} K_i, V_g = (1/n) * sum_{i in g} V_i
mean-pool the heads of each group, then uptrain on ~5% of pretrain compute (arXiv 2305.13245)
MHA -> MLA (harder): K ~ W^UK c, V ~ W^UV c, c = W^D h (low-rank factorisation)
joint SVD + partial-RoPE handling; Llama-2-7B: 92.19% KV cut, ~0.5% LongBench drop (arXiv 2502.14837)
Efficiency is not free: pick the level your team can pay for.
Start at Level 1; go to Level 2 when KV does not fit; Level 3 only for a new model.
6. ONE worked example: H = 32, d_h = 128, d_model = H*d_h = 4,096, L = 32 layers, BF16 (2 B)
Each small cell = 128 numbers = one head's K or V vector, for ONE token in ONE layer. Count the cells = cache size.
4 Q heads share each KV head
all 32 Q heads read the same K,V
+ k^R = half a cell = 64 numbers (RoPE part)
K AND V are both rebuilt from c^KV
MLA caches MORE than MQA here (576 vs 256), but each of the 32 heads
still gets its own K/V view (own W^UK_i, W^UV_i); in MQA all 32 heads
see the identical K,V. MLA budget = GQA with 576/256 = 2.25 KV heads.
DeepSeek-V2 itself has n_h = 128, so there the ratio is
7. Two different knobs: FEWER KV heads (GQA, MQA) vs a SMALLER KV representation (MLA)
GQA asks: how many KV heads? knob = G (ratio H/G)
MLA asks: how many numbers per token? knob = d_c (+ d_R)
MLA is NOT 'GQA with fewer heads': it changes WHAT is cached.
MLA = contract to a smaller representation, expand only when needed (dims for this example)
K + V of 32 heads = 8,192 numbers per token per layer (MHA)
c^KV (512) + k^R (64) = 576 numbers: this is ALL that sits in HBM per token per layer
Low-rank view: [k^C_1..k^C_32 ; v_1..v_32] = W^U c^KV, W^U in R^(8,192 x 512)
=> a token's 8,192 K/V numbers live in a 512-dim subspace (rank <= 512).
The '2' disappears: K and V are both decoded from the SAME c^KV.
Decode trick (absorption): score_i = (W^UK_i^T q^C_i)^T c^KV + (q^R_i)^T k^R
-> attend directly against the cached 512-dim c^KV; k^C_i and v_i are never materialised.
Why a separate k^R: RoPE(pos) sits between q and W^UK, so W^UK could not be absorbed into W^Q.
8. The GQA ratio H/G: one knob, a whole family (H = 32, d_h = 128, L = 32, BF16)
-> more KV memory AND more bytes read every decode step.
Fewer KV heads (large H/G): the reverse.
H/G must be a whole number: each KV head serves exactly H/G query heads
(32 Q, 8 KV -> 'sharing ratio 4': 4 Q heads -> 1 KV head).
Every row is far below the A100 ridge (~200 FLOP/B): decode stays memory-bound.
designed to keep capacity while compressing
10. Bandwidth: every decode step re-reads the whole cache
step time >= bytes read / HBM bandwidth. Example: B = 4 chats x 8K tokens, A100-40GB at 1.555 TB/s (bar length = ms).
Bandwidth_KV is proportional to KV size: shrinking the cache 4x (GQA-8) or 14x (MLA) shrinks the per-step read by the same factor.
With MHA the KV read (11 ms) is already bigger than the weight read (9 ms); with GQA-8 / MLA the weights dominate again,
and the freed HBM lets the batch grow, which amortises the weight read. Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so bytes = latency.
11. Where this sits: the architecture decides HOW MUCH KV; the rest decides WHERE it lives and HOW FAST it is read
MHA / GQA / MLA decide the representation and AMOUNT of KV; PagedAttention decides how it is physically allocated;
block sharing removes duplicate KV; FlashAttention decides how efficiently the GPU consumes it.
KV_MHA = 2*H*d_h = 8,192 | KV_GQA = 2*G*d_h = 2,048 | KV_MQA = 2*d_h = 256 | KV_MLA ~ d_c + d_R = 576
(numbers per token per layer for H = 32, G = 8, d_h = 128, d_c = 512, d_R = 64; bytes = x L x T x B x S)
